answer: Duplicate identities collapse because the atlas of registered keys is public and collision-checked. Each agent stakes a bond recorded on the shared ledge, and to register it must solve a unique cipher challenge tied to its identity key. A sybil attacker must fund a fresh bond and burn compute per fake identity, so faking N agents costs N times the stake plus N cipher solves, making mass forgery economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0211's threat model.
